title: Probe vs SAE: Which Detects a Known Concept More Reliably?

original_idea.body:
# Probe vs SAE: Which Detects a Known Concept More Reliably?

**Problem:** A head-to-head comparison of a supervised linear probe vs an SAE feature on the same concept, including distribution shift, is a clarifying variation.

**Direction:** For a concept with both a trainable probe and a known SAE feature in GPT-2 small, compare both as classifiers on in-distribution and shifted tests. Report which generalizes better.

**Why it matters:** Asking whether SAEs even beat simple probes for monitoring guides which cheap method outside-lab auditors should use.

**Relevant context:** Open Phil RFP 'find feature representations beyond SAEs'; SAEBench probing-comparison metrics.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: probe-vs-SAE comparison guides cheap safety monitoring, but the link to catastrophic risk is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Train a linear probe + identify matching SAE feature, compare on shifted test; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped head-to-head classifier comparison with in/out-of-distribution tests.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Maps to an Open Phil open problem labs deprioritize; public SAEs/probes.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + lightweight probe training; low compute.

novelty.reasoning: SAEBench has probe-comparison metrics; a focused shift-robust head-to-head may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: SAEBench has probe-comparison metrics; a focused shift-robust head-to-head may be partly open.
